summary: Kickoff for Spruce Wellness onboarding to Redwood. Covered goals, success criteria, initial pilot scope (chat and embeddings for internal search), high-level architecture options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security requirements (SSO/SAML, SOC2, data residency), and next steps to enable a pilot in November. Agreement to run a technical deep dive and share SSO and network details.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-02 16:00 PST | Duration: 60m | Attendees: Liam Chen, Priya Patel, Marco Ruiz (Redwood) / Dana Morgan, Ethan Park, Riley Torres (Spruce)

[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Liam, AE on the account, with Priya our CSM and Marco our solutions engineer.
[00:18] Dana: Thanks Liam. Hi all, Dana here, Head of ML at Spruce. We mainly want to get the pilot started and understand what pieces you need from us.
[00:28] Liam: Great, quick agenda — align on outcomes & success criteria, walk through pilot scope, network/security checklist, and agree next steps. Sound ok?
[00:38] Ethan: Yep that works. We have 45-60 minutes.
[00:45] Marco: Cool. I'll kick off with the pilot scope then. So from Redwood side, typical quick win is embeddings for search and a chat assistant integration. For the pilot you mentioned internal search and triage?
[00:58] Dana: Yeah internal knowledge search and a small chat workflow to help triage support tickets, nothing customer-facing yet. Latency is important but not ultra low, more like interactive.
[01:12] Marco: Perfect. For that workload we usually recommend starting on Hosted API to iterate quickly — you get streaming, function-calling, and we've got pre-curated models that work well for embeddings and retrieval. If you need data isolation we can discuss Dedicated or Private later.
[01:30] Riley: Quick question around data — anything we send to Hosted persist? We have PHI-ish records and want to avoid retention.
[01:37] Priya: Good callout. By default Hosted API has configurable retention; for regulated data we often recommend Dedicated or Private deployment and encryption with customer-managed KMS. We can walk through retention controls and audit logs.
[01:50] Ethan: We are SOC 2 Type II in progress and need audit logs and SAML SSO.
[01:56] Marco: We support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and detailed audit logs. Private deployment gives you control plane in your VPC if you need on-prem style isolation, but Dedicated can also meet many enterprise needs with VPC peering and dedicated GPU pools.
[02:12] Speaker 1: Sorry, can you repeat the KMS part?
[02:15] Priya: Sure — we integrate with customer KMS providers for encryption at rest. For Private or Dedicated you can bring your keys; hosted can also be configured depending on the contract.
[02:26] Dana: For timeline — we want the pilot live in two weeks ideally, is that realistic?
[02:32] Marco: Two weeks is aggressive but doable for a narrow scope if you can provide SAML metadata, allowlist IPs or peering details, and a sample dataset. We'll supply an SDK snippet and a short checklist.
[02:44] Liam: We'll also send the onboarding deck and a high-level project timeline after this call.
[02:50] Riley: Networking — we run on AWS in us-west-2, EKS, and we have strict egress rules. We prefer VPC peering over open allowlists.
[03:01] Marco: VPC peering is supported; for Hosted we can do private link in many cases or peering for Dedicated. We'll need your VPC info and contact for networking.
[03:12] Ethan: Who from Redwood handles the peering?
[03:15] Priya: That would be me and our infra team; Marco will own the technical details. We'll coordinate with your network engineer.
[03:24] Marco: Also, small note on throughput — embeddings are CPU-light but chat inference token cost matters. For cost control we recommend prefix caching and batching config; we'll include Optimize recommendations for your query patterns.
[03:40] Dana: Good, budget is a concern so we need clear cost estimates for pilot vs production.
[03:45] Liam: We'll provide example cost scenarios: Hosted pay-as-you-go for exploration, and a Dedicated pool estimate for sustained usage.
[03:54] Dana: Ok. On the security checklist — SSO, SOC2 certs, penetration test reports?
[04:00] Riley: And we need to know retention policy options and how to purge data.
[04:06] Marco: We can share SOC2 and pen test summaries and a retention/erase flow. For Hosted we have configurable retention windows; for Dedicated/Private you can set strict retention and control logs.
[04:18] Speaker 2: Is there any compliance docs publicly available?
[04:21] Priya: Yes, we'll share our security binder link and an internal doc with the SSO/KMS network checklist.
[04:29] Dana: Great. For success criteria — what's the acceptance for pilot?
[04:33] Liam: We propose: 1) embeddings result in >10% improvement in retrieval MRR on internal queries, 2) chat reduces triage time by 20% on sampled tickets, 3) infra integration completed w/o security blockers. If that aligns we can finalize.
[04:49] Dana: That sounds reasonable. We'll validate with product.
[04:53] Marco: On instrumentation — we provide per-route latency and token cost dashboards; we can set up a trial dashboard for you to watch pilot metrics.
[05:03] Ethan: Will we get logs at token level?
[05:06] Priya: Yes, token-level cost and request traces are available, plus audit logs for user actions.
[05:12] Riley: For SSO, we prefer SAML but open to OIDC. Our IdP supports both.
[05:18] Marco: Either works — we'll take SAML metadata as a first step.
[05:22] Dana: Anything else we need to provide today?
[05:25] Marco: To keep the two-week timeline: SAML metadata, network contact and VPC peering/allowlist details, short sample dataset, and an owner for the pilot.
[05:36] Liam: I'll circulate a follow-up with those asks and schedule the technical deep dive.
[05:40] Dana: Thanks, one more question — if we later need on-prem, how painful is migration?
[05:46] Marco: We design rollouts so model versions and routing are portable. Private deployment will take more lead time but the API surface stays consistent so client code changes are minimal.
[05:58] Ethan: Ok good.
[06:00] Priya: I'll add the milestones: kickoff, infra setup, pilot run, metrics review. We'll put dates in the doc.
[06:08] Liam: Any blockers?
[06:10] Riley: Not on our side — need to confirm schedule with network team.
[06:14] Dana: We'll aim to get SAML and network contacts by Friday.
[06:18] Liam: Perfect. Next steps recap — Priya sends onboarding deck + security binder, Marco schedules technical deep dive and shares SDK snippets, Spruce to provide SAML metadata and network contact.
[06:30] Speaker 1: Thanks everyone.
[06:32] Liam: Thanks all, we'll follow up.

Notes: transcription shows occasional speaker mislabels; minor mis-transcribed product terms (e.g., "Redwood Dedicat" in one segment but clarified). Shared artifacts: onboarding deck (link sent after call), security binder (link), initial pilot checklist (link).
